item.title: Why Rebuildability Beats Reviews
item.description: Reviews tell you how a product felt in week one. Rebuildability tells you what it costs in year five. On Durable Picks we grade every boot, tool, and kitchen essential on five checkable points: full grain upper, stitched sole attachment, a non foam midsole, a replaceable heel stack, and a real recraft path. A stapled sole fails point two every time. If a cobbler can undo the stitching and start over, you buy one pair a decade. If the heel is glued, the clock is already running. That rubric, not the star rating, is how durablepicks dot com ranks what earns the words buy it for life.

item.title: The Five Point Rubric in Ten Minutes
item.description: Here is the whole inspection in ten minutes. One: turn the product over and find the seam where the sole meets the upper. Stitched means rebuildable, glued means disposable. Two: press the midsole. Leather or dense cork passes; foam that crushes in a year fails. Three: check the heel. A stacked leather heel with a replaceable top lift is the cheapest part to fix and the first to wear. Four: look up the maker's recraft program or confirm any cobbler can service it. Five: run the math: a forty dollar scoop resoled twice beats four disposable replacements. Five passes means the listing earns a spot on durablepicks dot com.
